recipes.name: Gouda and Spinach Stuffed Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound fresh spinach, rinsed and torn into bite-size pieces
0.5 teaspoon Creole seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Coat a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Lay each pork chop flat on a cutting board. Use a sharp knife held parallel to the board to cut a deep pocket into each chop, leaving three sides intact. Fill each pocket with spinach, then cheese.
Place panko crumbs in a shallow dish. Spread a thin layer of horseradish over each chop, then roll in crumbs to coat. Arrange chops in the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle with Creole seasoning.
Bake in the preheated oven until brown and crispy, about 45 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into pork should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Gouda and Spinach Stuffed Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Delicious stuffed and breaded pork chops made with six ingredients - thick-cut pork chops, smoked gouda, fresh spinach, horseradish mustard, panko crumbs, and Creole-style seasoning.

video.description: Elevate your pork chop dinner into the truly sublime with these delicious stuffed chops! After slicing a pocket into each chop, stuff with fresh spinach and smoked Gouda cheese. Coat lightly with horseradish, then roll in crispy panko crumbs and finish with Creole seasoning. Bake until browned, crispy and temptingly melty inside.  With prep so quick and simple and cook time out of hand, what are you waiting for? A great dish for hectic weekdays or impressing pork chop-loving guests!

review.reviewBody: I used thick cut loin chops. The 40 minutes in a 400 oven concerned me so I browned them in a skillet and then finished them at 350 for about 20 min. The internal temp was 160 when they came out. Absolutely wonderful.

Made horseradish mustard by using equal parts of Dijon mustard and horseradish. Stuffed the chops with the cheese and spinach and some of the mustard mixture, salt and pepper. Didn't use the creole seasoning. Used half Italian seasoned bread crumbs and half Panko with some Paprika. Browned in a frying pan and finished in the oven at 375 for 15 minutes. Perfect!

These were absolutely delicious. I purchased Inglehoffer deli mustard with horeseradish roots as it was the only horseradish mustard that wasn't in a gallon container. It was a winner! I've never tasted such a delicious mustard taste. I put a generous tablespoon on top of each chop and then patted the crumbs on as the other reviewer suggested. I used 4 oz of spinach and it filled the chops plenty. I used a good brand of smoked gouda. I bought the bone in chops as I think these are always tastier. Cutting the pouch was the hardest part (sometimes you can find them already cut). The recipe is easy and would be a great weeknight dinner. Even bone in, they take less than 45 minutes to bake. I served them with pearl couscous and apple sauce. This will be one of my favorite meals in the future. I inserted a small metal kitchen pick in the opening to keep the stuffing in. The little bit that came out got browned and crispy and was wonderful. I recommend using the panko crumbs because they turned out so good. We definitely could taste the mustard throughout the breading. I was generous with it and the brand was awesome. If you want to try a recipe, follow the instructions and don't add watery mushrooms to dilute the other flavors. I don't understand why people rate something that they have changed dramatically.

Excellent dish! I made a mixture in the food processor of grated cheese and fresh spinach with a bit of olive oil to make it sort of spreadable. I pounded boneless pork sirloin chops until they were evenly thin, spread the mixture on each chop, then rolled each one up and secured the edges with toothpicks. You can still coat these with the horseradish and crumbs before baking. 45 minutes is way too long. I suggest baking them at 350 and start checking them after about 20 minutes or so. I used a 350 convection for 20 minutes and they were completely done inside and crispy outside from the convection air movement. I don't know how a regular oven works for this dish.

My wife described this as the best Pork Chops she has ever had. Like other in reviews, I seared the meat in a skillet and put it on a roasting pan so it was less greasy. Also, I bought the pork chops before I found the recipe, and they were thin cut. To work around this, I lined up the bones in pairs, breaded on one side of each piece and sandwiched the spinach and cheese between them. I kind of liked this, as it allowed me to put a lot more spinach in, which was a great for sneaking vegetables in on kids.

This was the best meal! I modified it to my taste used garlic mustard, and Ritz crackers for the crust. Rubbed inside and out with salt,pepper, garlic. use plenty of creole seasoning. Pat dry with towel to help the crust stick. Close with a toothpick. Honestly the best thing I've ever made!

Usually the first time I tried a recipe I'd made it as written. This time, however, I made a few minor changes since I did not have all the ingredients on hand for the thick pork chops. I brushed the pocket with a stone ground mustard, then stuffed it with spinach and the Gouda cheese. I did not have any bread crumbs so I just simply sprinkled the chops with a generous amount of the creole seasoning. They were then put on a grill, and they came out unbelievably moist and tasty. This recipe is definitely a keeper, next time, I'll try it as written. Thanks for sharing the recipe. I'll try it again with chicken breasts. Otherwise, an excellent recipe and much easier than I thought.

BUT had to do much tweaking. Sautee the spinach in garlic, olive oil salt and black pepper first. Take out of the pan and put in mixing bowl, then add shredded 18 month aged gouda, mix together then stuff. We also browned them before baking. Dipped in our own blend of bread crumbs and spices then baked. Still took about 30min in the oven. Made lots of juice. We just took them out and let them rest a bit. Served with Sautéed sugar snap peas and seasoned Basmati rice. Fantastic dinner for our little get together.

This was delicious! I ommitted the horseradish/mustard because my husband doesn't like it and instead used an egg wash before coating with panko crumbs. I baked on a cooling rack atop a cookie sheet and turned half way through baking so the panko was crispy on both sides. Thank you!

This was really tasty. I followed the ingredients (chose Panko, bone-in 1-inch pork chops) but after reading the reviews, decided to coat the inside of the pork pocket with the mustard before putting in the spinach and gouda. The inside was nice and moist. I used much more mustard than the recipe called for but it was worth it. The flavor mellows and it's not spicy. I also made sure to use the cajun seasoning on the outside and it was just the right bite. I did end up increasing the temperature to 425 to speed up cooking (which was about 50 minutes). I will definitely make again but wanted to warn those of you if you're going to make this for guests, make sure to allow time.

I wonder if this would be good with fruit also, like dried cranberries, apples? Might add that sweet to the savory...

My guests and I liked this recipe. I served it with garlic smashed red potatoes and green beans. I cut my own chops from a whole pork loin and made them 1 1/2" thick. I cut the pocket so that the "fat side" was on the bottom. This worked well because I could stand up the chops for stuffing and baking. At 400 they cooked in 25 minutes. I lightly sauteed the spinach in olive oil to add more moisture and didn't use as much cheese. I also couldn't get the panko to brown as much as I like. Next time I may lightly coat the it with cooking spray before I put them in the oven.
I followed the recipe except I had smoked Gouda jalapeno cheese instead of regular Gouda. Excellent taste combination.
EASY TO FOLLOW

I used a garlic butter cream sauce from Kinders to lightly coat the outside of the porkchop instead of horseradish mustard. baked on a rack in a casserole dish it was great. Or you can back in the casserole dish without the wire rack and not put panko crumbs on bottom of pork chop.
It was absolutely delicious, my wife loved it and incredibly easy to make!

Didn't have stuffing chops but wanted to try this! We used a meat mallet to flatten out regular boneless chops, covered one side in the horseradish mustard and bread crumbs, and rolled up the spinach and Gouda cheese cheese pinwheel style, held it all together with a toothpicks. Baked at 400 for 30 min. LOVED IT!
Perfect blend of flavors and the pork was amazingly moist. I followed the recipe as written. Give this a try and you won’t regret it.
Very awesome! Tender and juicy! I didn't have Gouda, so I hand grated sharp cheddar cheese, sprinkled Parmesan cheese on top. It was Yummy 😋
Made this exactly as stated. The chops were very tasty & had a nice crunch. I personally will marinate them as well next time as my particular chops weren't that tender.

This was great! I did slightly deviate from the recipe. I already had stuffed porkchops in freezer. I had stuffed them with cornbread stuffing when I had cut up a large pork loin. I didn't have horseradish sauce. However, I had horseradish mustard. It turned out really good. I cooked them for 45 minutes at 400. The internal temp was 160. I should had checked earlier because I was shooting for low 150's. It was still perfectly cooked. The stuffing kept it really moist. I loved it! The Cajun spices were a nice touch.
